the britholite minerals from the Keivy complex are a result of the complex interaction of alkaline fluids emanating from a magmatic system with the host rocks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the formation of britholite-group minerals in the Keivy alkali granitic-nepheline syentic complex, Kola peninsula, NW Russia, and with the chemical and mineralogical characteristics of these minerals.
the mineralogy, paragenesis, chemistry, and formation conditions of britholites from the Keivy alkali granites and nepheline syenites.
the formation of REE-rich lithology and the britholite mineralization, the REE and F distribution in britholite, and the fluid composition in different REE-rich rocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
britholite is a mineral that is not restricted to the REE-rich pegmatites of the alkaline complexes.

the britholite mineral group in the Keivy complex is a result of a complex sequence of processes involving magmatic, late- magmatic, and post- magmatic (hydrothermal, metasomatic) stages, and that the britholithes are the products of complex fluid evolution in a system with high F and variable CO2 contents.

the britholite-group minerals from the Keivy alkali granitoids and nepheline syenites are the products of magmatic, hydrothermal, metasomatic, and pegmatitic processes, with a wide range of compositions, depending on the chemical composition of the fluids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the britholite mineralization is a result of complex processes in the alkali granite-nepeline syenite magmatic system and its interaction with country rocks, and that the britholithes are the result of a complex chemical evolution of the magmatic fluids.
the britholite-group minerals are a very sensitive indicator of the chemical composition of the emanating fluids.

the REE and acti-nides distribution in host-rocks indicates that the emanation fluids were alkaline with significant amounts of fluorine and carbonic acid, which is in good agreement with the britholite composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
britholite is not only a mineral of REE deposits, but can be used as a mineralogical indicator for the presence of REE in the magmatic-hydrothermal system.
the REE-rich lithology of the Keivy complex contains numerous britholite occurrences, with different chemical composition and paragenesis.
britholite-group minerals can be used to constrain the composition of fluids involved in the formation of REE-rich rocks.
